tests.decision_rule: Revise or reject any novelty claim if a close source already gives the same trigger, scope, and transition remedy; cite and compare exact passages in the later probe.

tests.question: Can informed, fair, reversible specialization defeat the duty even when provider conduct caused recipients to stop checking?
cases_to_compare: clear risk disclosure plus retained usable fallback
clear disclosure but no feasible alternative or retained records
provider encourages abandonment and controls all evidence needed for re-entry
recipient independently chooses specialization without provider encouragement
tests.decision_rule: If informed consent alone defeats all cases, narrow the claim to coercive or unfairly structured dependence; if the duty survives, defend why the chosen risk could not include the impaired evaluative capacity.

tests.question: Does the epistemic criterion add anything to a general duty to repair dependence?
paired_cases: financial dependence caused by a provider, with evaluative capacity intact
evaluative capacity impaired by provider assurance, with no financial loss
both financial and epistemic dependence caused
neither dependence caused, but recipients rely heavily
tests.decision_rule: State what changes in duty-bearer, remedy, or threshold across pairs. If nothing changes, drop the distinct-duty framing and present only a domain-specific application of general repair.

tests.question: Can 'minimum usable capacity to assess a successor' be specified without requiring an undefined level of self-sufficiency?
candidate_measures: notice while a fallback remains usable
tests.decision_rule: Identify a domain-relative threshold and cost limit; reject or narrow the proposal if the threshold cannot be made intelligible or proportionate.

probe_requirement: A later fresh probe must perform and archive actual source retrieval and reading before claiming any novelty assessment.
